issues.body: `migration_owned` still represents provenance as a set of bd-ids and requires exactly one marker-bearing issue for an id. If a legitimate pre-label issue is authenticated by its migration title and write-author contract, an unprivileged attacker can add a second issue with the same marker. `migration_owned` then omits the id, and `_marker_index` authenticates neither issue, causing `missing_issues` and a failed `--verify`. The added decoy-beside-real test is not a regression test for this path because `full` gives the legitimate issue `MIGRATION_LABEL`, independently authenticating it.
issues.fix_hint: Represent migration-owned provenance at issue granularity, such as authenticated `(bd-id, issue-number)` pairs, and have `_marker_index` authenticate only that exact legacy issue. Add a focused test containing an unlabeled, non-checkpointed issue with the valid migration title/write-author provenance plus an unprivileged duplicate marker; verification must remain clean while reporting only the duplicate under `unauthenticated_markers`.
issues.title: A decoy still invalidates legitimate pre-label migration-owned provenance

verdict.summary: Round 4 is stagnant: the round-3 provenance-granularity defect remains unchanged. `migration_owned` still returns only bd-ids and rejects an id whenever any second marker-bearing issue exists, while `_marker_index` authenticates legacy issues via `bid in owned`. An unprivileged duplicate marker therefore removes the legitimate pre-label issue's only authentication channel and makes an otherwise correct migration fail verification. The new tests still cover a decoy beside a label-authenticated issue, not a legitimate unlabeled migration-owned issue beside a decoy.
